reasons: Only 33 of 52 sections were reviewed. The rest, mostly the phone menu and menu button styles, has not been checked.
The font link ties the look to an outside service.
The active-page highlight class is not set in the header code shown, so the current page may not be highlighted.
No automated checks are visible. Styles are checked only by looking at the pages.

terms.meaning: The language that sets how a web page looks, such as colors, sizes and spacing.
A name attached to page elements so that a style rule can target them.
A named value, such as a color, that many style rules can share. Its name starts with two dashes.
A style rule that applies only when the screen is within a certain width.
A layout method that arranges items into rows and columns.
A set of colors chosen for light or dark mode.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Font loading
sections.what: Loads the Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts from Google. These fonts are used for most text on the site.
sections.why: Gives the site its typeface and monospace look.
sections.watch_out: If Google's font service is blocked, the page falls back to standard system fonts.

sections.name: :root, [data-theme="light"]
sections.title: Light mode colors and shared values
sections.what: Defines named colors for light mode, plus font names, corner roundness and animation speed. Other styles refer to these names instead of raw colors.
sections.why: Allows the look to change in one place.
sections.watch_out: Names such as the background primary value must stay defined, because many rules depend on them.

sections.name: [data-theme="dark"]
sections.title: Dark mode color overrides and base reset
sections.what: Replaces the light color names with dark ones when the page is in dark mode. Also resets default spacing on every element so layouts start from zero.
sections.why: Lets the same styles work in both themes.
sections.watch_out: Because of the reset, elements have no default spacing, so new layouts must add spacing explicitly. Any new color name added to light mode must also be added here.

sections.name: html, body
sections.title: Base page settings
sections.what: Sets the page background, text color, default font and size, and line spacing. Also stops sideways scrolling.
sections.why: Gives every page the same starting look.
sections.watch_out: Stopping sideways scroll can cut off wide content, such as large tables, instead of letting the user scroll to it.

sections.name: .label
sections.title: Label style and page width
sections.what: Styles small uppercase monospace labels. Also sets three page widths: the standard container, a narrow one for reading, and a full-width one.
sections.why: Consistent captions and layout widths.
sections.watch_out: The standard container stops at 1800 pixels, so very wide screens show empty margins.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 1024px)
sections.title: Medium screen padding
sections.what: On medium-width screens, reduces the side padding of the containers.
sections.why: Keeps content from feeling cramped on tablets.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 640px)
sections.title: Phone padding and one-column rule
sections.what: On phone-width screens, reduces container padding further and forces the ingest grid into one column.
sections.why: Fits content to small screens.
sections.watch_out: The ingest grid class is not styled in this file, so the one-column rule only matters where that class is used.

sections.name: .header
sections.title: Top bar
sections.what: Keeps the top bar fixed at the top while scrolling, with a bottom line and background.
sections.why: Keeps navigation always reachable.
sections.watch_out: Pop-ups and menus need a higher layer value, or they will slip behind the top bar.

sections.name: .header-inner
sections.title: Top bar layout
sections.what: Places the logo on the left and the navigation on the right in one row.
sections.why: Standard header arrangement.

sections.name: .logo
sections.title: Logo and navigation row style
sections.what: Styles the logo as heavy monospace text, with the second part in the accent color. Also lays out the navigation list as a row with spacing.
sections.why: Gives the app a branded look.
sections.watch_out: In light mode the accent color is almost the same as the main text color, so the logo highlight is subtle.

sections.name: .nav a
sections.title: Navigation link style
sections.what: Styles navigation links as small uppercase monospace text, grey by default and the accent color on hover or when marked active.
sections.why: Shows which page the user is on.
sections.watch_out: The active class is not set anywhere in the header code shown, so the current page may not be highlighted.

sections.name: .stats-bar
sections.title: Summary strip grid
sections.what: Arranges summary boxes in a six-column grid with thin dividers.
sections.why: Shows key counts at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Adding a seventh item will wrap it onto a new row on desktop.

sections.name: .stat
sections.title: Summary box
sections.what: Gives one summary item a background and centered padding.
sections.why: Makes each summary item look like a card.

sections.name: .stat-value
sections.title: Large summary number
sections.what: Styles the big number in a summary box with a light, large monospace font.
sections.why: Emphasizes the figure.

sections.name: .stat-label
sections.title: Summary caption
sections.what: Styles the small uppercase grey caption under a summary number.
sections.why: Labels the number.

sections.name: .pipeline
sections.title: Pipeline board grid
sections.what: Lays out the pipeline columns in a responsive grid where each column is at least 220 pixels wide.
sections.why: Columns fit the screen and wrap when space runs out.

sections.name: .column
sections.title: Pipeline column box
sections.what: Gives each pipeline column a background, border, rounded corners and a minimum height of 200 pixels.
sections.why: Makes each stage visible as a distinct column.

sections.name: .column-header
sections.title: Column top row
sections.what: Lays out the top row of a column with padding and a bottom line, with the title on the left and the count on the right.
sections.why: Clear column heading.

sections.name: .column-title
sections.title: Column title text
sections.what: Styles the column title as small uppercase grey monospace text.
sections.why: Consistent heading look.

sections.name: .column-count
sections.title: Column count badge
sections.what: Styles the number of items in a column as a small badge.
sections.why: Shows how many items a stage holds.

sections.name: .column-body
sections.title: Column item spacing
sections.what: Sets padding and vertical spacing for the cards inside a column.
sections.why: Keeps cards evenly spaced.

sections.name: .card
sections.title: Application card
sections.what: Styles a clickable card with a border, rounded corners, padding and smooth color changes.
sections.why: Each application is shown as a card.

sections.name: .card:hover
sections.title: Card hover highlight
sections.what: On hover, darkens the card's border and shifts its background to the hover shade.
sections.why: Shows the card is clickable.

sections.name: .card-company
sections.title: Company name on card
sections.what: Styles the company name as medium-weight uppercase monospace text.
sections.why: Makes the company the most prominent line.

sections.name: .card-role
sections.title: Job title on card
sections.what: Styles the job title in regular sans-serif text, in the secondary color, with space below.
sections.why: Secondary to the company name.

sections.name: .card-meta
sections.title: Card footer row
sections.what: Lays out the bottom row of a card with items centered and spaced apart.
sections.why: Arranges status and other details neatly.

sections.name: .card-location
sections.title: Location text on card
sections.what: Styles the location as small uppercase grey monospace text.
sections.why: Quiet secondary detail.

sections.name: .pill
sections.title: Status badges and colors
sections.what: Styles a small outlined tag and gives each status its own color: sourced, reviewed, applied, interview, offer and rejected.
sections.why: Status can be recognized at a glance.
sections.watch_out: A status without a matching color rule shows as a plain tag. The archived status has a color variable but no badge rule, so it will not get this styling.

sections.name: .score
sections.title: Score row and bar colors
sections.what: Styles the score row: filled bar blocks in the accent color, empty blocks in the border color, and the number in the secondary color.
sections.why: Matches the score display in the components file.
sections.watch_out: The score bar class names are used by the score display component, so renaming them there breaks this styling.

sections.name: .btn
sections.title: Button styles
sections.what: Styles the standard button as an outlined, small uppercase monospace button that inverts on hover. Also defines primary (filled) and secondary variants.
sections.why: Keeps every button looking the same.
sections.watch_out: Button text color is taken from the page background color, so changing one color can make button text hard to read.

sections.name: .section-header
sections.title: Section header bar
sections.what: Lays out a section's heading row with the title on the left, controls on the right and a bottom line.
sections.why: Consistent section headings.

sections.name: .section-title
sections.title: Section title and empty message style
sections.what: Styles section titles as small uppercase monospace text. Also styles the empty-state box, centered and grey, for lists with nothing in them.
sections.why: Consistent headings and empty messages.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 768px)
sections.title: Tablet grid rules and page layout helpers
sections.what: On medium screens, shows the summary strip in three columns and stacks the pipeline into one column. Also defines the page shell and main area layout used by pages, which apply at all sizes.
sections.why: Keeps wide grids usable on tablets and gives pages a consistent frame.
sections.watch_out: The page shell and main area rules sit outside the medium-screen rule, so they apply at every width.

sections.name: .surface-card
sections.title: Basic card panel style
sections.what: Gives a plain rounded box with a background, a thin border and inner padding. Many content blocks on the site use this look.
sections.why: Gives the site one shared card style so panels look consistent.
sections.watch_out: The mobile rules later in this file reduce the padding, so the card looks different on small screens.

sections.name: .surface-card-accent
sections.title: Highlighted card panel style
sections.what: Same card look as the basic panel, but with an accent-colored border to draw attention to a key item.
sections.why: Lets the site highlight important panels without a separate design.
sections.watch_out: The accent color comes from the theme blocks at the top of this file, so it changes with light or dark mode.

sections.name: .skill-bar-track
sections.title: Skill bar background
sections.what: Draws the thin grey track behind a skill level bar.
sections.why: Likely reason: the rounded, hidden overflow keeps the colored fill inside the track's rounded edges.
sections.watch_out: The track is only 4 pixels tall, so changing its height makes the bar much heavier.

sections.name: .skill-bar-fill
sections.title: Skill bar colored fill
sections.what: Draws the colored part of a skill bar and animates its width over about 0.6 seconds when it changes.
sections.why: The short animation makes skill level changes easy to notice.
sections.watch_out: This class only styles the fill; the width must be set by the component that uses it.

sections.name: .skill-card
sections.title: Skill card style
sections.what: Gives each skill its own card with a border, padding and a short color transition on hover.
sections.why: Keeps each skill visually separate from its neighbors.
sections.watch_out: Nothing visible here; the transition only affects border and background colors.

sections.name: .skill-card:hover
sections.title: Skill card hover and priority colors
sections.what: Brightens the border of a skill card when hovered, and adds a colored left edge for critical, high, medium or low priority.
sections.why: The left edge color lets users see priority at a glance.
sections.watch_out: The priority colors only appear if the component adds these exact class names.

sections.name: .level-badge
sections.title: Skill level tags
sections.what: Styles the small monospace tag that shows a skill level, with a separate color for novice, intermediate, advanced and expert.
sections.why: The color steps show growing level without extra text.
sections.watch_out: The level class names must match the level values in the data exactly, including lowercase spelling.

sections.name: .pipeline-wide
sections.title: Wide grid layout for pipeline
sections.what: Arranges items in a grid of columns at least 260 pixels wide, adding columns as the screen gets wider.
sections.why: Lets the pipeline cards fill the screen and wrap onto new rows automatically.
sections.watch_out: On very narrow screens a single column is the only option, because each column needs at least 260 pixels.

sections.name: .app-two-col
sections.title: Two-column page layout
sections.what: Splits the page into a wide main column and a narrower side column, with a 24 pixel gap.
sections.why: Lets the main content and a side panel sit next to each other on wide screens.
sections.watch_out: The mobile rule that stacks these columns lives in a later media block, so both places must change together.

sections.name: .projects-grid
sections.title: Two-column project grid
sections.what: Shows project cards in two equal columns with a small gap.
sections.why: Fits more project cards on the screen at once.
sections.watch_out: A later mobile rule switches this to one column, so check both rules when changing it.

sections.name: .config-grid
sections.title: Two-column settings grid
sections.what: Puts settings sections in two equal columns with space below.
sections.why: Keeps the settings page compact on wide screens.
sections.watch_out: A mobile rule later in the file makes this one column.

sections.name: .add-company-grid
sections.title: Three-column add-company form
sections.what: Places the fields of the add-company form in three equal columns.
sections.why: Keeps the form short and easy to scan.
sections.watch_out: A mobile rule later in the file makes this one column.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 768px)
sections.title: Tablet layout and long-text protection
sections.what: Stacks the add-company, project and settings grids into one column on screens 768 pixels or narrower. Also makes long words, code blocks and links wrap, and shrinks images to fit their box. Sets the desktop menu to show and the mobile menu controls to hide.
sections.why: Long text, wide code blocks and images could otherwise push content off the screen.
sections.watch_out: The desktop menu is shown by default here, and a later mobile rule hides it, so do not assume the default is the final state.

sections.name: .hamburger-btn
sections.title: Menu button box
sections.what: Styles the square outlined button that opens the mobile menu, with three stacked lines inside.
sections.why: Gives phone users a familiar menu button in place of the full navigation bar.
sections.watch_out: The button is only visible on small screens because its wrapper is hidden on wide screens.

sections.name: .hamburger-line
sections.title: Menu button lines
sections.what: Draws each of the three thin lines inside the menu button.
sections.why: The three lines form the standard menu icon.
sections.watch_out: Each line is only 1.5 pixels tall, so it can be hard to see on low-resolution screens.

sections.name: .mobile-menu
sections.title: Mobile menu panel
sections.what: Shows a full-width dropdown panel under the header, with a border, shadow and a layer above page content.
sections.why: Holds the navigation links when the desktop menu is hidden.
sections.watch_out: The panel is positioned against the header, so the header must stay relatively positioned for it to line up.

sections.name: .mobile-menu-item
sections.title: Mobile menu links
sections.what: Styles each link in the mobile menu as a full-width row with padding, a divider line and a hover highlight.
sections.why: Makes each link easy to tap on a phone.
sections.watch_out: The last-item rule removes the divider from the final link, so adding a non-link item at the end can look odd.

sections.name: .mobile-menu-footer
sections.title: Mobile menu footer row
sections.what: Lays out a row at the bottom of the mobile menu with items spread to the two ends and a top divider.
sections.why: Likely reason: holds small controls at the bottom of the menu, such as a theme switch. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Nothing in this section shows what goes in the footer, so check the component that uses it before changing this.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 768px)
sections.title: Phone layout rules
sections.what: On screens 768 pixels or narrower, shows the menu button, hides the desktop menu, makes the header a positioning base for the dropdown, stacks the two-column layout, sets stats to two columns, reduces container padding, and shrinks buttons and cards.
sections.why: Changes the whole page to fit a phone without separate page code.
sections.watch_out: Several earlier rules at the same 768 pixel width are spread through this file, so a breakpoint change must be made in every block.

summary: The shared stylesheet that sets colors, fonts, spacing and the common look of buttons, cards, labels and layouts for every page, with light and dark themes.
purpose: Keeps the app's look consistent by defining named colors and reusable style classes in one place.
why: Likely reason: lets every page share one theme, so colors can be changed in one spot. The reason for putting everything in one file is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Loads the Inter and JetBrains Mono fonts. 2. Defines the light color names and other shared values. 3. Overrides the color names for dark mode and resets default spacing. 4. Sets base page styles. 5. Defines reusable classes for the header, navigation, summary strip, pipeline columns, cards, buttons, labels and the phone menu. Media rules change the layout for smaller screens.
inputs: The class names used in page and component code, and the theme setting on the page.
outputs: The visual look of every page, in light and dark mode and at phone and tablet sizes.
risks: Fonts load from Google's servers, so the look depends on that service. Changing one color name affects every page that uses it. Only the first 33 of the file's 52 sections were reviewed for these notes.
debug: If colors look wrong, check the theme setting on the page and the color names in the light and dark blocks. If a page looks cramped on a phone or stretched on a tablet, check the media rules. If fonts look wrong, check the font link at the top and whether Google's service is reachable. If a class seems to do nothing, search the code for that class name, since a spelling mismatch is a common cause.
